Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.24% today to close at $478.07, extending a strong two-week rally of 13.2%. The gain reflects the broader energy backdrop: U.S. crude oil has climbed above $101 per barrel as Iran escalates attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil supply. Refineries across the U.S. are running at 93.5% capacity, and the combination of tighter crude supplies and strong refining demand is supporting margins for companies like Marathon that process crude into fuel.

The two-week surge reflects deeper market nervousness about oil supply disruptions. Tanker rates have spiked significantly enough that traders are now pricing crude with a $30–$40 premium just to account for the cost and risk of physically delivering it—well above the headline price. This kind of supply tension typically benefits refiners, who can buy crude at one price and sell the finished gasoline and diesel at higher spreads, even as Middle East geopolitical risk keeps crude prices elevated.
